postings.title: Lead Scientist, Protein Engineering
postings.text:
What We're Building:
We have been quietly building the foundational layers of our Physical AI Scientist platform:

- Our team is opinionated and straightforward. We don’t mind intense discussions about design tradeoffs. If we have arguments or miscommunication, we resolve conflicts quickly and empathetically.
About the Role
We're seeking an exceptional antibody or protein scientist to drive the scientific backbone of our Physical AI Scientist platform. This role combines deep technical ownership, scientific execution and leadership, and cross-disciplinary collaboration in a fast-moving environment. As a founding member of this team, you’ll work with a high-impact team of engineers to help establish Medra as the leader in Physical AI to close-the-loop between computational predictions and experimental validation in biologics R&D.
In this role, you will:
- Work with our internal engineering team to design and launch Medra Labs 1
- Define and set-up the workflow for end-to-end antibody and protein engineering, including liaising with vendors & suppliers, setting up instruments, testing hardware / software prototypes, and final integration into robust, production-grade systems
- Develop fit-for-purpose assays to evaluate binding, specificity, potency, and developability (e.g., SPR/BLI, ELISA, cell-based assays, stability screens).
- Design and execute iterative experimental campaigns that balance speed, rigor, and scalability.
- Troubleshoot complex experimental challenges and set best practices for reproducible, high-quality data generation.
- Drive the creative process to uncover novel opportunities in instrumentation, workflow design, and system integrations.
- Work closely with customers to deeply understand their science, define scientific goals and requirements, outline a fully-automated experimental plan, and run experiments
- Provide technical leadership in antibody/protein engineering across internal teams and external partners.
- Contribute to scientific strategy, mentoring, and the evolution of Medra’s Physical AI platform
Let's talk if you have:
- PhD in Bio/Biological Engineering, Biological Sciences, Protein Engineering, Biophysics, Chemistry/Biochemistry, or a related field
- 3+ years of direct hands-on experience with the design and characterization of antibody and protein therapeutics, including cloning, expression, purification, analytics, and quality control. Experience with at least one advanced modality (beyond monoclonals) is preferred.
- Experience with binding and developability assays such as SPR/BLI, ELISA, flow cytometry, stability, etc., as well as the relevant instruments for each.
- Proven ability to design clear experimental plans, think strategically, solve complex problems creatively, and communicate effectively with diverse stakeholders, including scientists and senior executives
- Entrepreneurial drive and a desire to have broad ownership, operating with significant autonomy in a highly ambiguous and rapidly changing environment, akin to a startup CSO
- A willingness to wear many hats / a flexible attitude towards responsibilities and scope
- Bonus points if you have experience working with available AI models for protein generation and prediction
This position is 100% in-person , you must be able to come on-site to our San Francisco office. We do not offer hybrid roles. We do offer relocation benefits for applicants who need to relocate.
What we offer:
- 401k
- Medical insurance
- Dental Insurance
- Relocation benefits
- Unlimited PTO
- Weekday dinners

BizOps at Medra:
The Business Operations role is dynamic, offering intense learning and growth opportunities. You’ll work directly with the Chief of Staff to scale Medra’s processes and turn vision into execution, bringing operational rigor to our most pressing priorities. Some reasons you might be interested in the role:
- You’re excited by robotics, LLMs, and the chance to apply cutting-edge technology to real world problems.
- You’re driven by impact, with bold ambitions to tackle meaningful challenges (like accelerating the discovery of new cancer treatments).
- You want to grow fast by taking on a lot of responsibility.
Responsibilities
- Business Operations: own execution and documentation of day-to-day processes, tackling ad-hoc problems, keeping the office operating smoothly. Help plan events such as happy hours, off-sites, recruiting events, marketing events.
- Finance: own expense management, invoices & receivables, taxes, and financial modeling.
- People Operations: facilitate onboarding, payroll, cap table management, and be a leader who sets the culture at Medra.
- Process Improvement: identify root causes of pain points and streamlining cross-functional workflows and tooling across customer success, hiring, finance, and ops.
- Special Projects & Strategic Initiatives: act as Medra’s “Swiss‑army knife,” scoping and executing on some of the company’s most pressing challenges on an ad-hoc basis.
Requirements
- 1-3 years of experience in strategy consulting, finance, product, or business development is very useful. We are very open to high-slope individuals at the beginning of their professional career.
- Get stuff done: Even though you are juggling a million balls at once, you do what you say you’re going to do, on time, every time. No task is too small for you and you’re ready to do whatever it takes.
- Comfort with ambiguity, lack of structure, and lack of clear guidelines.
- Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills (verbal and written).
- Direct, willing to take feedback gracefully, and unafraid of giving feedback openly .
- Adaptive and introspective; willing to learn, teach, lead, and follow.
Bonus points for:
- Experience leading operations at high-growth, early-stage tech companies.
- Experience in applied math, statistics, engineering, the sciences is a huge plus.
- Built internal knowledge bases or no‑code automations that saved colleagues hours per week.
- Has owned financial reporting, taxes, or vendor contracts.

🤖 Physical AI that can operate scientific instruments with human-level dexterity.
🧪 Scientific AI that can analyze results, reason about next steps, and close the loop autonomously.
This is an incredibly ambitious mission, but we believe that a team of ambitious people with high ownership can accomplish incredible things.
The Team:
• We're a team of passionate, mission-driven engineers and scientists from companies like Tesla, Amazon, SpaceX, and Neuralink. We're collaborative and love moving fast, both with our product and on team trips skiing or go-karting!
• As a team, we love nerding out about engineering and robotics — plus other topics like race cars or cooking. We like learning new things and then sharing our new knowledge with each other.
• Our team is opinionated and straightforward. We don't mind intense discussions about design tradeoffs. If we have arguments or miscommunication, we resolve conflicts quickly and empathetically.
The Role:
We're looking for a Systems Test Engineer - Summer 2026 Internship to be our front line of robot uptime at a customer site in Boston. You'll work on-site to monitor daily protocol runs, respond to issues in real time, keep the system running smoothly and help engineering team prioritize and ship improvements.
This is a high-impact role where your reliability directly enables cutting-edge biological research. You'll work independently on-site while staying tightly connected to Medra's engineering team (in San Francisco) via Slack and our observability tooling.
In this role, you will:
- Maintain robot uptime and reliability across daily protocol runs, ensuring the system performs at peak efficiency
- Diagnose and resolve operational issues onsite using SOPs, playbooks, and your own intuition for the system
- Escalate complex issues to the engineering team with clear, structured incident reports including relevant metadata
- Monitor system health proactively using dashboards and alerting tools to catch issues before they cause production failures
- Perform routine calibration checks and preventive maintenance on the robot, peripherals, and consumables
- Document all incidents, resolutions, and observations to build a reliable knowledge base of site-specific issues and drive data-driven improvements over time
- Support remote and on-site engineering visits by assisting with hardware upgrades, validating software deployments, and performing test runs after changes
- Collaborate cross-functionally with customer scientists to coordinate run schedules and communicate system status
Let's talk if you have:
- Background in robotics, automation, or mechatronics
- Comfort around automation equipment — you should be able to follow SOPs, troubleshoot basic hardware/software issues, and know when to escalate
- Strong written communication — you'll be filing incident reports and coordinating with software and hardware engineers daily
- A dependable, detail-oriented approach with a bias toward documenting what you see and proactively flagging potential issues
- Willingness to be on-call or adjust schedule to support critical customer runs when needed
(OPTIONAL) Bonus points if you have:
- Familiarity with life science lab equipment
- Experience with observability or monitoring tools (dashboards, alerting systems, log analysis)
- 1+ years of experience in a manufacturing support, field engineering, QA, or production support roles

The Role:
We’re looking for a highly organized, scrappy, and people-focused Office Manager to own the day-to-day operations of our San Francisco office. This person will be the backbone of the workplace experience: keeping the office running smoothly, supporting employees onsite, coordinating vendors and facilities, managing meals and snacks, and helping bring a new space to life as the company grows.
This person will play a critical role in shaping the employee experience and helping our office scale thoughtfully as we grow. We’re looking for someone who can bring order, energy, and ownership to the workplace and create an environment where the team can do their best work.
In This Role, You Will:
- Own daily office operations for our San Francisco office
- Partner with a designer to help set up and operationalize a new office space
- Manage facilities-related needs, including maintenance requests, office upkeep, and landlord coordination
- Serve as the main point of contact for building issues such as HVAC, access, repairs, and other workplace needs
- Manage vendor relationships across office services, supplies, meals, maintenance, and related partners
- Coordinate employee onboarding logistics, including workspace readiness, access setup, and general day-one experience
- Support basic IT and workplace technology coordination, including office devices, access systems, and troubleshooting with external partners as needed
- Administer office systems and tools such as badge access and Ring
- Oversee meal ordering, snack programs, and kitchen stocking
- Handle mail, deliveries, and package receiving
- Open doors for visitors, deliveries, and service providers as needed
- Maintain a clean, organized, and welcoming office environment
- Anticipate operational gaps and solve problems quickly with minimal direction
Let’s Talk If You Have:
- Experience in an Office Manager or similar workplace/office operations role
- Strong organizational skills and excellent attention to detail
- Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and keep things moving in a high-velocity environment
- Highly autonomous and resourceful; able to identify what needs to happen and make it happen
- Strong project management instincts and follow-through
- Comfortable being hands-on with day-to-day office needs
- Clear communicator with strong interpersonal skills
- Positive, service-oriented mindset with a willingness to jump in wherever needed
- Handy, practical, and scrappy approach to problem-solving
(OPTIONAL) Bonus Points If You Have:
- Experience with facilities coordination
- Experience planning office events or team gatherings
- Experience supporting an office build-out, move, or new space setup in partnership with external vendors or design teams
- Familiarity with tools such as Slack, Google Workspace, badge access systems, and Ring
